justification: Developer tooling only. No product code, no served output, no database read or write, no migration. Two new scripts plus an observation-mode reporting block in scripts/qa_gate.py that never touches the passed/failed verdict, and one blocking line in .githooks/pre-push whose trigger condition cannot false-positive. Not Minor, because scripts/falsifiability.py is now the thing every falsifiability claim in this campaign rests on, and a defect in it makes every downstream proof worthless; not Critical, because nothing here can reach a customer, a report or a row.

falsifiable_check.fails_when: TWENTY planted defects were each confirmed to turn this command red, then restored byte-identically -- and the planting was done BY the new helper, driven from an unmutated copy of itself in a temp directory so the file being mutated was never the file doing the mutating. On scripts/falsifiability.py: disabling the post-write hash comparison; making a missing anchor return instead of raise, which is the open-coded behaviour this replaces; downgrading the restore assertion to the print that PR #883 actually shipped (2 failures); removing the CRLF anchor translation so a multi-line plant silently no-ops again; skipping the recovery sidecar (4 failures); and swapping the atomic os.link claim for a non-exclusive os.replace. On scripts/doc_claims.py: check_paths returning [] (10 failures), check_versions returning nothing (6), check_dependencies returning nothing (8), dropping the stale-line-citation check, ignoring the basename-ambiguity flag so a route.ts:548 claim is judged against an arbitrary route.ts, rewording an unknowable note as an all-clear, counting markdown as evidence that a requirements file is installed, accepting a bare `-r file.txt` with no pip install in front of it (48 failures), guessing which number belongs to which identifier when a line names two, dropping the backslash-continuation join so a real multi-line pip install reads as an orphan, weakening the ast test-import parse so pytest.importorskip is missed, replacing the ast version parse with a raw-text regex so a constant inside a comment becomes a live value, removing the GIT_* environment scrub so git answers about the wrong repository, and taking the baseline counts from all violations instead of the ones written. Baseline green before each plant and green again after; both files' final sha256 byte-identical to the first. ONE MUTANT INITIALLY SURVIVED and is recorded rather than quietly fixed: swapping os.link for os.replace left every test passing, because the concurrency test was reaching StalePlantFound through the up-front sidecar.exists() check and could not distinguish an atomic claim from check-then-act. It was a test that could not fail for the reason it claimed. Rewritten to force the lost race -- exists() reports False for a sidecar that is present -- after which it dies. The authority is external to the code under test in the two cases that matter most: tests/test_doc_claims.py::test_planting_a_nonexistent_test_path_goes_red and ::test_planting_a_mismatched_version_goes_red plant into the real tracked docs/QA-DATA-PROVENANCE.md and assert against the real filesystem and the real code constants, not against a fixture the check also generated.
falsifiable_check.external_authority: git ls-files and the filesystem decide whether a path resolves; the assignment statements in tracked .py/.ts/.tsx files decide what a version constant holds; the pip install -r lines in .github/workflows and Dockerfiles decide which requirements files are installed. None of the three is produced by doc_claims.py, so no check compares the tool against its own output.

pre_impl.existing_data: Four sweeps against origin/main 704ccb0f, recorded in each script's prior-art-checked header. No shared plant-restore helper exists: git ls-files scripts/ matching falsif|plant|restore|mutat returns only mutation_health.py and run_mutation_tests.sh, which drive mutmut and never edit a file in place; git grep for planted-a-defect phrasing across py/ts/tsx/sh/md/json returns zero; git grep for def plant|restore|prove_falsif returns zero. The only implementation that has ever existed is a throwaway scratchpad script from PR #883, never committed. Nothing checks a document's claims against code either: the three existing lint_*.py scripts all lint code, and the plan doc's own section 4i says of this exact idea 'Noted, not yet machinery.'
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: Three of the brief's factual claims did not survive checking, and one correction changed the design. The brief says PR #883 'did it correctly with sha256 on both sides'. It hashes both sides but does not ASSERT either: a missing anchor prints '!! SKIPPED' and continues (scratchpad prove_it_fails.py:74-76), and the closing byte-identity comparison is print('BYTE-IDENTICAL TO BASELINE:', after == baseline) at line 94 -- it reports False and still exits 0. So the reference implementation fails open on BOTH rules, not neither, which is why the helper raises rather than reporting. The brief also implies these scripts are committed somewhere; they are not, in any branch. And the plan doc's section 4j claims the METHODOLOGY_VERSION single-source fix and the API score exclusion are 'SHIPPED' -- git grep METHODOLOGY_VERSION on origin/main returns zero and merged #887 touched five files, none of them code. That work sits in open PR #889, which is a different session's branch and was left alone.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: New shared helper rather than extending anything, because there is nothing to extend. The CRLF failure mode was verified rather than assumed: git config core.autocrlf is true on this repo, so every checked-out source file has CRLF endings while every anchor typed into a Python literal has LF, which makes the silent no-op the DEFAULT outcome of the naive pattern and not an unlucky edge case. That is pinned as its own test. The doc-claim check is added to the existing scripts/qa_gate.py rather than becoming a new gate, and reuses the committed-baseline idiom already established by scripts/check_dependency_skips.py.

functions.name: planted
functions.input: a file path, an anchor string or bytes, and its replacement; everything is coerced to bytes, so there is no decode step to crash on
functions.output: a context manager yielding PlantInfo with the before and after sha256 digests and which newline style the anchor matched
functions.if_none: raises rather than returning; a missing anchor, an ambiguous anchor, a no-op replacement, a write that reverts and a stale sidecar are each a distinct exception with the reason named

functions.name: _restore
functions.input: the target path, the original bytes, the original digest, and the sidecar path holding a second copy of those bytes
functions.output: returns only after the file on disk hashes to the original value, at which point the sidecar is deleted
functions.if_none: retries one write for a transient lock, then raises RestoreFailed naming both digests and leaves the sidecar in place so --recover can finish the job

functions.name: check_dependencies
functions.input: the project directory and the set of tracked paths from git ls-files
functions.output: violations for requirements files no installer references and for packages tests import that the CI install set never provides
functions.if_none: when no CI pip install -r line can be found it emits an unknowable note and runs no test-import check, rather than reporting a clean result it did not earn

functions.name: observe_doc_claims
functions.input: the QA report path, the diff file list and the project directory, taken from the same argv parsing the gate already does
functions.output: a list of human-readable observation lines, diff-scoped to changed markdown plus the report itself and filtered against the committed baseline
functions.if_none: returns a SKIPPED line saying unknowable rather than an empty list, and never contributes to the errors list or the passed flag

values: N/A — no database or API values are read. The only external inputs are tracked file paths, file bytes and sha256 digests.
queries: N/A — no SQL is executed anywhere in this change.

break_it.scenario: A proof run is killed with SIGKILL or the machine loses power while a defect is planted, so the finally block never executes and the mutation stays in the working tree.
break_it.what_happens: The recovery sidecar written before the plant survives. The next planted() call on that file raises StalePlantFound and refuses to start, and .githooks/pre-push runs falsifiability.py --check, which exits 1 and blocks the push with the recover command in the message.
break_it.how: Sidecar written before the write and deleted only after a hash-verified restore; tests test_stale_sidecar_refuses_to_start, test_recover_restores_and_clears and test_check_cli_is_red_while_a_plant_is_live cover all three paths.
break_it.repro: python -m pytest tests/test_falsifiability.py -q -k 'stale or recover or check_cli'

break_it.scenario: Someone writes a multi-line anchor with LF newlines against this repo's CRLF working tree, exactly as happened when a plant silently no-opped and the run still reported success.
break_it.what_happens: The helper detects the file's dominant line ending, retries the anchor translated to it, and plants successfully with anchor_style CRLF-translated. If translation still finds nothing it raises PlantDidNotTake naming the line ending as the usual cause, instead of skipping.
break_it.how: dominant_newline plus _anchor_candidates; test_the_naive_pattern_is_the_one_that_no_ops pins the counterfactual that plain replace() is a no-op on the same input, so the reason survives even if the mechanism changes.
break_it.repro: python -m pytest tests/test_falsifiability.py -q -k 'naive or multiline or missing_anchor'

break_it.scenario: The restore write runs but a lock, an antivirus scanner or a filesystem layer leaves different bytes on disk, so the file looks restored and is not.
break_it.what_happens: RestoreFailed is raised with both digests. If the proof body ALSO raised, the restore failure is what propagates, because damage on disk outranks a failed assertion, and the body exception is preserved on __context__ so nothing is lost.
break_it.how: The finally block re-reads and re-hashes rather than trusting the write; test_restore_that_does_not_complete_raises and test_failed_restore_outranks_a_failing_body sabotage Path.write_bytes to force exactly this.

break_it.scenario: The doc-claim check reads a document that cites a bare route.ts:548 when forty-seven files share that basename, so the line-count comparison has no single file to judge against.
break_it.what_happens: The resolver returns an ambiguity flag alongside the match and the line-number comparison is skipped entirely. Reporting a line finding computed from an arbitrary same-named file would be a fabricated finding, which is worse than a missed one.
break_it.how: _resolvable returns a (path, unambiguous) pair and check_paths gates the lineref branch on it; test_line_citation_against_an_ambiguous_basename_is_not_reported covers it, and removing the flag turns the suite red.

break_it.scenario: The doc-claim check runs somewhere git cannot answer, for instance an exported tarball or a container without the .git directory, so no path can be resolved.
break_it.what_happens: scan returns zero violations WITH an unknowable note stating that no check ran and that this is not a pass, and observe_doc_claims prints a SKIPPED line. A silent empty result would read as a clean corpus.
break_it.how: tracked_files returns None rather than an empty set, and every unknowable branch appends a note; test_no_git_index_is_unknowable_not_clean asserts the note text, and rewording it as an all-clear turns the suite red.
break_it.repro: python -m pytest tests/test_doc_claims.py -q -k 'unknowable or unreadable or unmappable'

break_it.scenario: Somebody reads a quiet doc-claim run as evidence that a document is true, when the check cannot decide a semantic claim such as the services/CLAUDE.md sentence about which pipeline a product shares.
break_it.what_happens: Nothing is reported, because nothing decidable is wrong. The limit is stated in the module docstring, in the qa_gate observation footer and in the PR body, and a test builds a document whose every sentence is false but whose paths all resolve, asserting silence.
break_it.how: test_semantic_claims_are_out_of_scope pins the boundary so that a future widening has to change the stated scope deliberately rather than by accident.

break_it.scenario: The checker runs from inside a git hook, where git exports GIT_DIR and GIT_INDEX_FILE, and those variables override the cwd a subprocess was pointed at.
break_it.what_happens: Without a scrubbed environment `git ls-files` answers about the hook's repository instead of the scanned one, so every path resolves against the wrong file list. tracked_files now strips GIT_* before the call, and so does every git invocation in the test fixture.
break_it.how: doc_claims.git_env() removes GIT_* except the ssh/askpass helpers, and test_git_hook_env_does_not_redirect_the_file_list pins it by setting GIT_DIR to a different repository and asserting the scanned repo's files still come back.

mutation_analysis: Eleven mutations, all caught, listed with their failure counts in falsifiable_check.fails_when. The two that matter most are the ones reproducing real incidents: making a missing anchor return instead of raise reproduces the open-coded skip behaviour and goes red, and downgrading the restore assertion to a print reproduces exactly what PR #883 shipped and goes red with two failures. Two guards were confirmed load-bearing that a reviewer might read as defensive padding: removing the CRLF translation and removing the sidecar write both turn the suite red. Three defects in the new code were found by these tests rather than by review -- find was never converted to bytes so every plant raised TypeError, the code-constant regex used [Vv]ersion and therefore missed every SCREAMING_CASE constant including METHODOLOGY_VERSION, and the doc version regex refused a literal ending a sentence. Not covered by mutation testing: the argparse wiring in either main(), and the exact wording of finding messages. Sol raised five findings on the diff and all five were real and are fixed, each pinned by a new test: --strict exited 0 when the scan could not run at all, which is the fail-open this change exists to remove and now exits 2; pip's -r includes were not followed, so an included requirements file would have been reported as an orphan nothing installs; the baseline was generated before the QA report was rewritten and therefore carried fingerprints from the previous report; a version identifier defined in two modules let a doc name the other module's value unchallenged, now reported as an unknowable note while a literal no module holds is still a finding; and a file present on this machine but untracked was accepted as a resolved path, which made the result depend on whose checkout ran it. A second Sol round on the fixed diff raised five more, also all real and all fixed, each pinned by a test: the recovery sidecar was written non-atomically, so a kill mid-write could leave TRUNCATED bytes that --recover would then write over the target while reporting success -- a backup that can be silently wrong is worse than none, because it is trusted, and it is now a temp file plus fsync plus os.replace; the pre-push guard was gated on the helper file existing, which failed open in the one situation that matters, so the sidecar search now runs in shell and does not depend on the helper at all; markdown was counted as evidence that a requirements file is installed, meaning a README SAYING pip install -r was believed about what the code does, which is the precise error this module exists to catch, and dropping it surfaced requirements-latentscope.txt as a genuine orphan nothing automated installs; a commented-out install line counted as an install; and version constants were read by raw-text regex, so an assignment inside a comment or an example string was treated as a live value that could silently validate a false doc claim, now parsed with ast for Python and comment-stripped for TypeScript, where the residual string-literal gap is stated rather than papered over. A third round raised four more, again all real and all fixed: the sidecar was claimed by an exists() check followed by a create, which is check-then-act, so two concurrent plants on one file would both proceed and the first restore would delete the second's evidence -- the claim is now a single atomic os.link that raises FileExistsError, with the weaker os.replace kept only for filesystems without hard links and labelled as weaker; the directory entry was not fsynced, now best-effort with an explicit note that it is a no-op on Windows and that the kill case which actually happened is covered without it; the baseline header counted all violations while writing only the baselineable ones, so it could disagree with its own findings list; and a version literal was bound to EVERY identifier within the window rather than the nearest, which would fabricate two mismatches from the line 'API_VERSION 2.0 and METHODOLOGY_VERSION 1.1' when both claims are correct. That last one is the worst class in this change -- a fabricated finding -- and it is now pinned by a test in both directions. Three Sol rounds, fourteen findings, all real, none dismissed.
residual_risk: The doc-claim check's precision is measured, not assumed, and the number is a lower bound. The first live run produced 368 findings; six defects in the CHECK accounted for most of them -- an extension alternation matching ts before tsx, a missing trailing boundary turning shapely.geometry.shape into a .sh file, a lookbehind that let placeholder and glob tails through as _config.py and _parking.py, no relative-path resolution for ../.. references, ambiguous basenames driving line-count claims, and whole-line scoping that pulled a correlation threshold into a version claim. After fixing all six the corpus stands at 137 baselined findings across 124 documents -- 127 path, 1 version, 9 dependency -- plus 8 more raised against this change's own QA report, which is deliberately excluded from the baseline because it is rewritten every PR and a stale fingerprint would suppress the same false claim when a later report made it for real. Of the 127 path findings, 126 name a basename that exists nowhere in the repository, which makes them high-confidence true positives; a targeted sweep of the tokens that looked wrong found 3 false positives (an abbreviation _geometry.py, the prose fragment Check-exclusions.ts, and pdfplumber/pdf.js which names a third-party file outside the repo), so roughly 2.4 percent. A 15-item random sample contained none. That sweep was targeted rather than exhaustive, so 3 is a floor and not a measured total -- all 127 were not hand-verified, and saying so is the point of observation mode. Also unmeasured: whether the finding count grows or shrinks over a fortnight of normal commits, which is the number that would earn blocking status. Separately, the basename-keyed installer map cannot distinguish three different requirements.txt files, which is deliberate because Dockerfiles COPY-rename them, but it means a genuinely orphaned requirements.txt in a subdirectory would be missed. Thirty-five test imports could not be mapped to a distribution and were not checked; they are reported as unknowable, not as clean. One further false-positive mode was found by running the gate on THIS report: a document that QUOTES a nonexistent path as an example gets flagged for quoting it. Six of the six new findings on this change are that mode -- five are the false-positive examples named above and the sixth is the uncommitted scratchpad script prove_it_fails.py. It is the same shape as the CLIMATE_RISK_METHODOLOGY.md line that describes the v1.2 defect and is then reported for containing 1.2. Deliberately not suppressed: distinguishing a quoted example from a live claim needs a reader, and a heuristic that guessed would start hiding real findings. It is the strongest argument in this change for staying in observation mode. Found the hard way, and worth recording because it is this change's own subject matter: the first push attempt went red inside .githooks/pre-push while the same suite was green run directly. Git exports GIT_DIR and GIT_INDEX_FILE to its hooks and they override a subprocess's cwd, so the test fixture's `git init` and `git commit` operated on the REAL worktree -- moving its branch to the fixture's commit and replacing its index with six fixture files. Nothing was lost (the work commit was recovered by SHA with git reset --mixed, working tree untouched), and the same variable would have made `git ls-files` answer about the wrong repository, which is a silently wrong file list underneath every path finding. Both the tool and the fixture now scrub GIT_*, and the case is pinned by a test that points GIT_DIR at a different repository.

post_merge.db_reset: No. Nothing in this change reads or writes any database.
post_merge.secrets: No. No credentials, tokens or connection strings are read, written or logged.
post_merge.other_repo: No. Single repository, and the new pre-push line is guarded by a file-exists test so a clone without the script is unaffected.
post_merge.manual_verify: Yes. Run python scripts/doc_claims.py once after merge and confirm 138 findings against scripts/baselines/doc-claim-baseline.json, then git config core.hooksPath .githooks in each existing worktree so the planted-defect guard is actually installed rather than merely committed.
